disclaimer: Chiasm identification is interpretive - reasonable, careful readers propose different boundaries and centers, especially for a whole book. The Flood narrative and Jonah structures below are widely, though not universally, agreed on; the Leviticus and Revelation structures are each one defensible proposal among several competing ones in the literature. Treat the labeled center as the commentator's argued turning point, not an uncontested fact.

chiasms.title: The Flood Narrative
chiasms.scholarNote: Structure following Gordon J. Wenham, "The Coherence of the Flood Narrative," Vetus Testamentum 28 (1978), still the standard reference point for this reading.
chiasms.description: One of the cleanest large-scale chiasms in the Hebrew Bible: thirteen panels turning on a single hinge - "But God remembered Noah" - the moment the flood stops rising and starts receding.

chiasms.title: The Book of Leviticus
chiasms.scholarNote: A simplified version of structural readings advanced by Mary Douglas (Leviticus as Literature, 1999) and others, who argue the book's units are arranged concentrically around the Day of Atonement rather than merely topically listed.
chiasms.description: Leviticus is usually read as a topical law code, but its major sections can also be read as a ring composition centered on the Day of Atonement - the one day the high priest enters the Holy of Holies, at the literal middle of the book.

chiasms.title: The Book of Jonah
chiasms.scholarNote: A commonly taught reading; see e.g. the paired-panel outlines in the NIV/ESV Study Bible introductions to Jonah.
chiasms.description: Jonah's two flights from his calling - one physical, one emotional - frame the book: pagan sailors and pagan Nineveh both respond to Yahweh better than his own prophet does.

chiasms.title: The Book of Revelation
chiasms.scholarNote: One widely-taught simplified reading (broadly following Kenneth Strand's and others' seven-part chiastic proposals for Revelation's macrostructure) among several competing outlines - Revelation's structure is genuinely contested, and a purely linear/sequential reading is also common and defensible.
chiasms.description: On this reading, Revelation's seven-fold judgment series (seals, trumpets, bowls) frame a central vision of the real war behind the war: the dragon, the woman, and the beasts of chapters 12-14 - which is also thematically where this app's companion project, DISINHERITED, draws its spiritual-warfare premise.
